rationale.usefulness: Versioned migration details, memory options, server defaults and speech-format boundaries directly help builders of local apps, research tools and educational narration. Proposed acceptance sets are concrete and preserve model/engine/hardware distinctions. The report makes no unsupported installation, quality or speed claim.
rationale.impact: An explicit compatibility commitment in an established broadly used local-inference foundation is consequential for downstream applications. The release adds meaningful memory, model and server changes, but it is not the invention of local inference and does not guarantee model quality. Impact 7 places the 1,920-word body in the 1,800–2,200 band, subject to the final mean.
rationale.novelty: The public C API/ABI versioning boundary, new expert-cache controls and speech endpoint are useful differentiation for maintainers. They are evolutionary engineering features; existing inference architectures and a 1.0 label alone do not justify exceptional novelty.
rationale.maturity: The established project, tagged release, detailed build/server references and explicit compatibility limits show strong documented readiness. The transition removes APIs, backend/model behavior remains workload dependent, and tool/MCP surfaces retain experimental warnings. No native test was claimed by this report.
rationale.openness: The exact tagged engine is inspectable under standard MIT terms with portable C/C++ interfaces, multiple backends and versioned documentation. Model licenses and checkpoint reproducibility are separately required, and backend dependencies remain, so openness is high without asserting unrestricted rights to every supported model.
